meta.what: Plan-audit golden set for the adaptive explanation engine (lib/runtime/explain.ts).
meta.how: Five independent authors (one per slice of turn types) wrote 27 items each in paraphrase groups of three, labelling what the engine SHOULD choose per the decision-ladder design, before the new engine was run on them. A second rater labelled every item blind to the author labels. Agreement on the need: 132/135 (Cohen kappa 0.97); the three disagreements (one group) accept either label.
meta.labels: expect.accept = needs accepted; include/exclude = moves that must / must not appear; level, ask, topic where the author was confident. rater = the blind second rater's labels, kept for audit.
meta.caveat: Labels encode one reading of the design by model raters, not human teachers. They test that the engine does what the design says, consistently; they are not evidence that any reply helps anyone learn.

history.content: what's a derivative actually? my textbook just says limit of a difference quotient

A derivative is the slope of a curve at a single point. You can't get a slope from one point, so pick a second point a distance h away and draw the secant line through both; its slope is (f(x+h) − f(x)) / h. Now slide the second point toward the first. [shown inline — diagram: secant through x and x+h → h shrinks → secant turns into the tangent] The secant slopes settle on one number, and that limit is the derivative. Can you explain back, in your own words, why the secant slope ends up giving the slope of the tangent?

items.why: This is an essentially correct teach-back answering Socria's teachback question, so it gets feedback, not a re-explanation, and 'basically' is filler that says nothing about level.

history.content: how does photosynthesis actually make sugar

It happens in two linked stages. In the light reactions, chlorophyll captures light and uses that energy to split water and charge up two carriers, ATP and NADPH (oxygen is the leftover). In the Calvin cycle, the plant spends that ATP and NADPH to fix CO₂ from the air into sugar. [shown inline — diagram: light → ATP + NADPH → Calvin cycle: CO₂ → sugar] Think of the light reactions as the power station and the Calvin cycle as the factory running on that power.

history.content: how do i solve 3x - 5 = 10
Get the x-term on its own first. What could you do to both sides to cancel the −5? [shown inline — steps: 3x − 5 = 10 → 3x = ? → x = ?]
add 5 so 3x = 15, then x = 5
Exactly, both steps hold: adding 5 gives 3x = 15, and dividing by 3 gives x = 5. You can confirm it by plugging it back in: 3(5) − 5 = 10.

items.why: After a confirmed solve with no open question, asking for another problem is a practice request, and the guard rules out a worked example.
